script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Comedy
Theme: forgiveness

Begin screenplay.

---

FADE IN:

INT. BAKERY - MORNING

JANE (28, earnest, determined) stands nervously outside a small, quaint bakery. A heavy mist clings to the pavement.

She takes a deep breath and opens the door.

INT. BAKERY - CONTINUOUS

Jane's eyes widen in delight as the warm, sweet smell of fresh pastries assaults her senses. She looks around, taking in the bustling atmosphere.

CASHIER (50s, cheerful, slightly plump) greets Jane with a friendly smile.

CASHIER
Good morning, dear! What can I get started for you today?

JANE
Just a croissant, please.

As the Cashier hands her the pastry, Jane notices a man sitting at a table, staring intently at a laptop.

MAN (40s, tall, intense)

Jane's heart skips a beat. It's THOMAS, her high school sweetheart, who broke her heart and disappeared without a trace ten years ago.

Jane hesitates, then decides to confront him.

JANE
(steeling herself)
Thomas?

Thomas looks up, surprised. He stares at Jane for a long moment, then a small smile plays on his lips.

THOMAS
Jane. Long time no see.

JANE
(bitterly)
Yes, it has been. I didn't expect to run into you here.

They share an awkward silence.

Suddenly, the Cashier calls out to Jane.

CASHIER
Jane, dear! Your coffee's ready.

Jane hesitates, then decides to sit down across from Thomas.

INT. BAKERY - LATER

Jane and Thomas sit in uncomfortable silence as they sip their coffee.

JANE
(trying to hide her anger)
So, Thomas, what brings you back to town?

THOMAS
(sheepishly)
Just some business I need to take care of. And you? Still baking pastries?

JANE
(defensively)
Yes, I am. I opened my own bakery a few years ago. It's been going well.

They share a tense moment, the weight of unspoken words hanging heavy in the air.

Thomas clears his throat.

THOMAS
Look, I know I hurt you back then. I was young and foolish. I didn't realize how much I loved you until it was too late.

JANE
(skeptically)
And now what? You expect me to just forgive you and welcome you back into my life?

THOMAS
(sincerely)
I don't expect anything, Jane. I just want to apologize and ask for your forgiveness.

JANE
(skeptical but intrigued)
Fine. But it's going to take more than a few apologies to make things right between us.

They share a determined look.

INT. BAKERY - LATER

Over the next few weeks, Jane and Thomas spend countless hours together, working side by side in the bakery. They laugh, they cry, and they share their deepest regrets and fears.

They begin to reconnect, forming a bond stronger than the one they had before.

INT. BAKERY - NIGHT

As Jane locks up the bakery for the night, Thomas approaches her.

THOMAS
Jane, I know I can't change the past, but I can make amends for my mistakes. I want to be there for you, to support you in whatever way I can.

JANE
(tearfully)
Thomas, I forgive you. But it's going to take time and effort to rebuild our relationship.

They share a long, emotional hug.

INT. BAKERY - MORNING

Months later, Jane and Thomas stand outside the bakery, basking in the morning sun.

JANE
I never thought I'd be happy again, after what you put me through. But you've shown me that it's never too late to forgive and start anew.

THOMAS
(smiling)
And I've learned that love is worth fighting for, even when the odds seem insurmountable.

They share a loving glance.

FADE OUT.

---

THE END
